data.title: Close the Loop Reaffirms Earnings Outlook with Lower Debt and Tighter Cost Maintenance
data.description:
Close the Loop has opened FY27 with $32.4 million in first-quarter revenue and $4.3m in EBITDA, as its two operating divisions returned positive contributions.

The recycling and sustainable packaging group reaffirmed its $14m to $16m EBITDA guidance for the year to June 2027 after both divisions contributed to the September-quarter result.

Australian resource recovery operations recorded their strongest first quarter in three years, benefiting from higher-margin programs and tighter cost controls.

Its balance sheet has undergone a sharper change, with net debt falling from $38.1m at 30 June to $16.3m at 30 September following the settlement of convertible notes.

A refinancing approved by Citi Bank promises a further lift to cash flow through lower interest costs and smaller scheduled debt repayments, although the agreement has yet to be completed.

Packaging Order Momentum

Packaging generated $18.6m in quarterly revenue, helped by new Australian customer wins and an order book extending into the second and third quarters.

South African reel-stock orders strengthened in September, although port delays pushed some revenue into later periods, while the New Zealand operation is now running as a standalone business.

“Over the past 12 months, we have realigned the group around our core strength, exited underperforming businesses that did not align with our profitability and return objectives, settled our convertible notes, and materially reduced net debt,” chair Grant Carman said.

“Our priorities are now to drive profitable growth, strengthen cash generation, reduce debt, and ensure each division has the leadership, capability, and clear accountability needed to deliver sustainable returns.”

A new sorting project and increased deliveries helped Resource Recovery generate $13.8m across its European operations, while US demand for recycled resin improved alongside processing capacity and automation, following the restructuring of the plastics recycling business.

Financial Breathing Room

Close the Loop settled $24.4m of convertible notes after the June year end by issuing 60.4 million shares, a move that accounted for much of the subsequent reduction in net debt.

The proposed replacement of its existing PGIM debt facility has now received Citi Bank approval, with documentation and completion targeted for mid-December.

On the terms outlined, the interest rate would fall by about 450 basis points and annual interest costs by approximately $1.4m, with smaller quarterly principal repayments freeing up additional cash for operations and debt reduction.

A further US$2.5m payment is expected when the transaction closes, adding another near-term consideration to the group’s cash planning.

Leadership Team Changes

The $14m to $16m FY27 EBITDA target represents projected growth of 13% to 29% on the previous financial year.

Capital expenditure is forecast at $1m to $3m, compared with $2.5m last year, as the group prioritises cash generation and profitable growth.

Changes to the board see Trifon Dimos become chair after the annual general meeting, with Mr Carman to remain as a non-executive director.

As the business moves beyond its recent restructuring, management is reviewing divisional leadership and resources while directing investment towards operations capable of generating sustainable returns.

data.title: Nalco signs pact with Russia’s Rusal to study recovery of scandium from red mud
data.description:
State-owned Nalco on Wednesday said it has partnered with Russian firm Rusal to study the recovery of scandium from red mud generated during alumina production.

As India intensifies efforts towards securing strategic mineral resources for emerging technologies and clean energy applications, the partnership is expected to facilitate knowledge exchange and evaluation of viable pathways for scandium recovery from red mud, Nalco said in an exchange filing.

Rusal, a leading firm in the global aluminium industry and the world's largest producer of low-carbon aluminium, has developed technology for the extraction of scandium from red mud, a by-product generated during alumina production, thereby presenting valuable opportunities for technology sharing and cooperation in the critical minerals sector.

An MoU was signed on the sidelines of the 44th International Conference and Exhibition ICSOBA 2026, Nalco said in the filing.

"National Aluminium Company Ltd... has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the RUSAL for collaboration in the recovery of the critical mineral Scandium from Red Mud," the PSU said.

The signing of the MoU took place in the presence of Nalco CMD Brijendra Pratap Singh; Jagdish Arora, Director (Projects & Technical); Viktor Mann, Technical Director, Rusal, and other senior officials of both firms.

National Aluminium Company Ltd is a 'Navratna' public sector undertaking (PSU) of the mines ministry. It is one of the country's largest bauxite, alumina, aluminium and power complex. Currently, the government owns a 51.28 per cent stake in Nalco.

data.title: Stocks to watch, Nov 19: Jio Financial Services, Bharat Forge, LT Foods, National Aluminium Company, Dalmia Bharat, Tonbo Imaging India
data.description:
Jio Financial Services Limited has invested ₹123 crore in Jio BlackRock Asset Management Private Limited, the 50:50 joint venture between the company and BlackRock. The investment was made through a rights issue on November 18, 2026, to fund the joint venture’s business operations. The company subscribed to and was allotted 12.30 crore shares at par value on a rights issue basis. BlackRock also subscribed (₹123 crore) to an equal number of shares, maintaining the 50:50 equity split in the joint venture.

Bharat Forge has invested ₹291 crore in its wholly owned subsidiary, Kalyani Strategic Systems Ltd (KSSL), through a rights issue, using proceeds from its qualified institutional placement (QIP). The company has been allotted 29.05 crore fully paid-up equity shares of Kalyani Strategic Systems at ₹10 apiece.

LT Foods, the home-grown FMCG company, which owns basmati rice brands Daawat and Royal, on Wednesday said it will acquire US-based packaged foods company MK Foods Holdings Inc for an enterprise value of $5.8 million (around ₹54.2 crore). The company said its US subsidiary LT Foods Americas Inc has entered into an agreement to acquire 100 per cent stake in MK Foods Holdings Inc, which owns the premium Indian-inspired food brand Maya Kaimal.

National Aluminium Company, which had signed a ​pact with Russian aluminium producer ‌Rusal, has opened new tab to study the recovery of scandium from red mud, as India seeks more access ​to minerals used in advanced ​industry and clean energy. The collaboration ​would focus on knowledge sharing ​and on assessing possible routes to extract scandium from red mud, a waste product ​from alumina refining.

Dalmia Bharat, the country’s fourth-largest cement maker, on Wednesday said its board will consider a proposal to buy back fully paid-up equity shares at its meeting scheduled for November 23. Though the company did not disclose details of the proposed buyback, including its size, price, number of shares to be repurchased, or mode of execution, it said the board is expected to consider these parameters at its meeting on November 23.

Tonbo Imaging India has received a supply contract valued at ₹35.62 crore from the Ministry of Defence, Government of India. The order carries a warranty of 24 months and includes an option clause and a repeat order clause, each for up to 50 per cent of the ordered quantity, exercisable at the sole discretion of the customer.

data.title: Dalian iron ore snaps six-session losing streak on lower arrivals
data.description:
By Emily Ou Yong

Iron ore futures rose on Thursday, as lower port arrivals offered some support, though falling hot metal output and widening mill margin losses limited gains.

The most-traded January iron ore contract on China's Dalian Commodity Exchange (DCE) snapped a six-session losing streak to trade 0.78% higher at 650 yuan ($97.49) a metric ton, as of 0200 GMT.

The benchmark December iron ore <SZZFZ6> on the Singapore Exchange was 0.41% higher at $88.05 a ton.

Futures and spot prices rebounded together, with lower arrivals offering interim support, though a single-day gain does not establish stronger procurement demand, said analysts from Shanghai Metals Market (SMM) in a note.

Traders are holding offers firm, they said, but hot metal output continues to fall and port stocks remain high, keeping fundamental pressure in place.

Three blast furnaces were under maintenance this week, mainly in Hebei and Hubei provinces, while environmental curbs in Handan city remain in place and furnaces in the northwest are set to halt ahead of the winter break, pointing to a further decline in hot metal output, showed SMM data.

Key steel enterprises produced hot metal at an average of 1.82 million tons a day in October, down 3.8% from September and 5.9% lower in total output from a year earlier, data from the China Iron and Steel Association showed.

Losses at mainstream mills in key steelmaking hub Tangshan widened this week after a sharp fall in billet prices, with ordinary square billets at 2,810 yuan a ton ex-factory on November 18, data from consultancy Mysteel showed.

Other steelmaking ingredients on the DCE fell, with coking coal NYMEX:ACT1! and coke (DCJcv1) down 1.56% and 0.73%, respectively.

Steel benchmarks on the Shanghai Futures Exchange were mixed. Rebar rose 0.51% and hot-rolled coil gained 0.45%, while stainless steel fell 1.63%.

($1 = 6.6676 Chinese yuan)

data.title: ‘Nothing Wrong With NVDA Or AI Trade’: Kenny Polcari Says Fed’s Inflation Concerns Are The Bigger Market Risk
data.description:
Key points:
  • Polcari said that comments from the Fed and its policymakers have sparked inflationary concerns. 
  • Fed Governor Christopher Waller said in an interview on Wednesday that the central bank needs to “shock people” with at least a half-percentage-point interest rate hike in December as inflationary concerns continue to mount.
  • A day earlier, St. Louis Fed president Alberto Musalem said that the Federal Reserve may need several rate hikes to control inflation ​and should act soon. 

The Dow Jones Industrial Average and the S&P 500 took a beating on Wednesday, ending the session in red following weakness in the AI trade after the Federal Reserve’s minutes.

Kenny Polcari, Partner and Chief Market Strategist at SlateStone Wealth, said that the weakness in the indexes could not be blamed on Nvidia Corp.’s (NVDA) falling prices or the AI trade, noting that the Fed’s comments have sparked inflationary concerns.

In a post on X, Polcari said, “I am NOT buying the NVDA weakness as the reason for the weakness today in the Dow and S&P - You can blame Fed Gov Waller and Fed Pres Musalem for their predictions of more aggressive rate hikes. There is nothing wrong with NVDA or the AI trade - Come on! It's ridiculous.”

Fed Flags AI Risk 

The central bank’s policymakers called artificial intelligence “a material source of inflation risk” in their latest minutes from the October meeting, adding that “off-balance-sheet leasing commitments and circular financing arrangements among AI-related firms could amplify losses if returns on AI investment were to disappoint.”

“In the months ahead, almost all participants judged that, under their baseline outlooks for inflation and the labor market, further action to raise the target range for the federal funds rate,” the minutes said, “would likely be appropriate, in order to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2% objective.”

Meanwhile, economist Peter Schiff said in a post on X, “Inflation has been the Fed's go-to policy tool. Whenever there was a problem in financial markets, the Fed created more inflation to solve it. But now too much inflation has itself become a problem. Will the Fed choose to worsen the inflation problem to bail out investors again?”

Policymakers See Further Hikes On The Cards

Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said in an interview with CNBC on Wednesday that the central bank needs to “shock people” with at least a half-percentage-point interest rate hike in the December meeting as inflationary concerns continue to mount.

“I’m very, very concerned about inflation. It’s kind of headed in the wrong direction, and it’s spreading out,” Waller said. “If you really want to get it down, you’ve got to start taking more aggressive actions.”

A day earlier, St. Louis Fed president Alberto Musalem said that the Federal Reserve may need several rate hikes to control inflation ​and should act soon.

"The economy will likely require several interest ​rate increases before the spring of 2027 ​to achieve price stability in a timely manner," ⁠Musalem said, noting that the current 3.75% to 4% target range is below the level it needs to be at to achieve the 2% inflation target.

Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco President Mary Daly also noted that further interest rate hikes will be needed to ensure inflation returns to the central bank's 2% target. However, Daly suggested adopting a more “measured pace” to evaluate shifting economic conditions.

How Is The Market Reacting?

The SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), which tracks the S&P 500 index, was up 0.48% in the overnight session late Wednesday after closing in the red. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits was ‘bullish’ at the time of writing.

The Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) also edged higher in the overnight session, with retail sentiment in the ‘bullish’ and ‘neutral’ territories respectively.

The iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF (TLT) was down 0.03% amid ‘bullish’ sentiment.

data.title: Vietnam, Russia leaders agree to deepen their energy cooperation at APEC
data.description:
Vietnam and Russia agreed to deepen cooperation in energy during talks between leaders of the two countries on the sideline of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, the Vietnamese government said.

  • Russian President Putin told Vietnamese President To Lam at the meeting on Wednesday that Moscow is willing to share energy development experience, technologies and help Vietnam with training, the government said in a statement

  • The two leaders discussed expanding collaboration in oil and gas, where Russian firms have been active in Vietnam for decades through joint ventures and offshore projects

  • They also agreed to promote new areas of cooperation, including renewable and nuclear energy development

  • Vietnam is moving ahead with plans to revive its civilian nuclear power program to meet soaring electricity demand

  • The two leaders also pledged to strengthen broader economic, trade and investment links

  • Russia this week staged its most significant deployment of military aircraft across East Asia in possibly more than a decade, coinciding with the APEC meeting, with flights by strategic bombers flanked ‌by long-range tankers that eventually landed in Vietnam’s Danang Airport

data.title: Malaysia to review leaked Deutsche Bank 1MDB files, task force official says
data.description:
Malaysia is studying leaked files that allegedly show that Deutsche Bank ignored internal red flags to help move millions of dollars linked to fugitive financier Low Taek Jho, a senior official said on Wednesday.

News portal Malaysiakini reported that Deutsche Bank's correspondent banking service was used to facilitate at least 24 transactions worth €172.98 million that were linked to Low, a key player in the multibillion-dollar 1Malaysia Development Berhad scandal.

  • The portal cited leaked internal files from the "Inside Deutsche Bank" investigation, which covers more than 15 million files dating from the early 2010s

  • The report also stated that the bank continued to process millions of euros in transfers linked to Low in 2015, despite filing its own suspicious activity reports

  • Reuters was unable to independently verify the documents

  • A spokesperson for Deutsche Bank said in an email response that the bank has cooperated fully with regulatory and law enforcement authorities in relation to inquiries concerning 1MDB, and has not been subject to any regulatory penalty or sanction arising from 1MDB

  • "As stated in asset forfeiture complaints filed by the US Department of Justice, 1MDB made material misrepresentations and omissions to Deutsche Bank officials in connection with 1MDB’s transactions with the bank," the spokesperson said

  • The chairman of the task force in charge of recovering 1MDB assets, Johari Abdul Ghani, told Reuters that the relevant parties, including the task force itself and 1MDB's legal team, were now studying the information

  • However, he said it was still "premature" to comment on Malaysia's position while the court case against Deutsche Bank was ongoing

  • "Malaysia has pursued, and will continue to pursue, action against international banks which we believe failed to carry out proper customer due diligence checks in relation to the movement of 1MDB funds by Low, his associates and/or proxies," he said

  • 1MDB is currently in settlement talks with Deutsche Bank over the legal dispute

  • Low has previously denied wrongdoing, and his current whereabouts are unknown

data.title: Here's why shares of United Spirits, Radico Khaitan, Allied Blenders will be in focus today
data.description:
Shares of alcohol beverage companies, including United Spirits Ltd., Radico Khaitan Ltd. and Allied Blenders and Distillers Ltd., are expected to trade lower on Thursday, November 19, after India imposed an effective customs duty of 162.5% on bulk Scotch whisky imports from the UK.

The effective levy is higher than the 150% duty that applied before the India-UK free trade agreement (FTA) came into force in July. The trade pact had halved the tariff on Scotch imports to 75%, a move that was widely seen as a major boost for companies such as Pernod Ricard and Diageo, which import Scotch in bulk and blend it with other spirits to manufacture whisky in India.

However, the tariff reduction has now become the subject of a dispute between Indian authorities and liquor companies over the classification of bulk Scotch imports.

Indian investigators have argued that bulk Scotch concentrates used in the manufacture of blended whisky should be classified under a separate customs category introduced in May, known as ‘compound alcoholic preparations’. This category attracts a 150% tariff, along with an additional consumption tax, taking the effective duty to 162.5%, according to a Reuters report.

The dispute has resulted in thousands of litres of bulk Scotch being held up at Indian ports. More than 80 shipping containers belonging to Pernod Ricard, Diageo and Bacardi have been detained, Reuters reported last week.

Under a provisional release arrangement pending the investigation, companies are required to pay duty equivalent to 75% of the goods' value upfront, with the remaining amount covered by bank guarantees, the report said.

Pernod Ricard, which owns UK-based Chivas Brothers, Diageo and other liquor companies operating in India believe that both bulk and bottled Scotch imports should attract the 75% tariff agreed under the trade pact.

The British government has repeatedly said it is engaging with New Delhi to resolve the issue, while Indian authorities have indicated that the dispute will be settled soon.

Pernod Ricard and Diageo have moved to arrange bank guarantees and other funding to secure the release of their detained containers and minimise disruptions to business. Bacardi, meanwhile, is still evaluating its next steps, Reuters reported.

Around 80% of Scotch whisky imports from Britain by volume arrive in bulk, making the classification issue particularly significant for the industry. India is the world's largest market for Scotch whisky by volume.

A large share of bulk Scotch imports is used to manufacture Indian-made foreign liquor (IMFL) whisky. These products are made by blending a proportion of Scotch with other spirits and are typically priced well below fully imported brands such as Chivas Regal and Johnnie Walker.

Whisky tariffs had been a key sticking point during the prolonged negotiations leading up to the India-UK trade agreement, which came into force on July 15. The UK had said that iconic British products, including Scotch whisky, would benefit from the pact.

The Scotch Whisky Association has estimated that the trade agreement could boost Scotch exports to India by $1.34 billion over five years.

data.title: U.S. Offers $50 Million to Support Malaysia's Sovereign AI Cloud Initiative
data.description:
By Ying Xian Wong

KUALA LUMPUR--The U.S. plans to help develop Malaysia's sovereign artificial-intelligence cloud, including through the participation of U.S. technology firms.

President Donald Trump and Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim announced the cooperation on Wednesday.

Trump is in Shenzhen this week as part of his visit to China for Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation meetings.

The U.S. indicated its intention to provided $50 million in financing for Malaysia's initiative, as well as technical assistance and training, the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission said.

The move comes as Malaysia seeks to establish itself as a regional AI hub, attracting billions of dollars in investment from global technology companies amid growing demand for computing power and cloud services.

In budget 2026, the government allocated 2 billion ringgit, or about $486 million, to establish the sovereign AI cloud, underscoring its push to build domestic AI infrastructure and ensure greater control over data and computing resources.

data.title: Why Is AMD Stock Rising Overnight?
data.description:
Key points:
  • OpenAI’s models helped deliver a 14% improvement in power, performance, and area (PPA) in AMD’s flagship chip design.
  • AMD stock rose over 0.3% in overnight trading, after gaining 5.3% in the regular session. 
  • Retail sentiment for AMD was ‘bullish’ as of late Wednesday.

OpenAI and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) on Wednesday hailed their collaboration, with the ChatGPT maker saying that its models helped improve AMD’s flagship chips.

The tweaks delivered up to a 14% improvement in power, performance, and area (PPA) over already optimized baselines for AMD’s flagship GPU design.

OpenAI described the work as roughly a year of chip-design progress achieved in less than five months, adding that AMD had already sent some model-designed changes for manufacturing.

Separately, commentators noted the use of AMD technology in ‘Grand Theft Auto VI,’ Rockstar Games’ highly anticipated title that was released overseas on Wednesday, giving another boost to the chipmaker’s market sentiment.

AMD shares rose 0.3% in overnight trading, after gaining 5.3% in the regular session.

How OpenAI Boosted AMD IP

The work focused on rewriting SystemVerilog, the code used to describe chip circuits, OpenAI detailed in a blog post. OpenAI models proposed changes to circuits that calculate, control operations and move data, with successful checks using Synopsys electronic design tools.

OpenAI said the same processes helped optimize its own custom inference chip, Jalapeño, and it is now applying the approach to third-party hardware.

“Proud of these fantastic results - @OpenAI + @AMD engineers pushing the frontiers of chip design together!” AMD CEO Lisa Su said in an X post.

OpenAI President Greg Brockman wrote: “roughly an additional year of progress on @AMD's chip achieved in less than 5 months using our models, with some of these results included in a design that's recently been taped out — unprecedented results at the frontier of chip design.”

AMD Tech Powered GTA 6 Image Upscaling

Rockstar told gaming and tech news site Wccftech that ‘GTA VI’ uses AMD’s FSR 4 upscaling on Xbox Series S. The game renders at 720p, and then FSR rebuilds the image at 1080p.

The Series S is the only console version confirmed to use AMD’s machine-learning upscaler and also supports ray-traced global illumination (RTGI), according to Wccftech.

AMD introduced FSR Upscaling 4.1.2 for Xbox Series X and Series S developers earlier this month through the Xbox Game Development Kit.

Retail View On AMD

On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment for AMD remained ‘bullish,’ unchanged from the previous day.

“AMD Another big success in a row for AMD. In the Grand Theft Auto (GTA) game that is breaking and will break all records, the processors, graphics cards, console chips, and image-scaling technologies are the work of AMD—setting new standards unattainable for the vast majority,” said a trader.

Another wrote: $AMD is going to be the next NVDA. Lisa please take us to join the 5T club.”

Year to date, AMD stock is up 148%.

data.title: Japanese Market Modestly Higher
data.description:
TOKYO (dpa-AFX) - The Japanese market is trading modestly higher on Thursday, extending the gains in the previous session, following the mixed cues from Wall Street overnight. The Nikkei 225 is moving above the 59,100 level, with gains in index heavyweights and technology stocks partially offset by weakness in financial stocks.

The benchmark Nikkei 225 Index is up 85.92 points or 0.15 percent to 59,110.26, after touching a high of 59,660.61 earlier. Japanese stocks ended modestly higher on Wednesday.

Market heavyweight SoftBank Group is gaining more than 3 percent and Uniqlo operator Fast Retailing is adding almost 2 percent. Among automakers, Toyota is edging up 0.1 percent, while Honda is edging down 0.1 percent.

In the tech space, Advantest is edging up 0.4 percent, Screen Holdings is adding almost 1 percent and Tokyo Electron is gaining more than 3 percent.

In the banking sector, Mizuho Financial is declining almost 2 percent, Sumitomo Mitsui Financial is losing almost 1 percent and Mitsubishi UFJ Financial is down more than 1 percent.

Among the major exporters, Mitsubishi Electric is edging down 0.3 percent and Panasonic is losing almost 2 percent, while Sony is adding more than 2 percent and Canon is gaining almost 1 percent.

Among other major gainers, Trend Micro is surging almost 6 percent, while J. Front Retailing, Lasertec and Nomura Research Institute are advancing more than 3 percent each. Daikin Industries and Terumo are gaining almost 3 percent each.

Conversely, JX Advanced Metals is tumbling more than 6 percent and Mitsubishi Materials is sliding almost 6 percent, while Sumitomo Metal Mining and Mitsui Kinzoku are slipping almost 5 percent each. Nissan Motor, Japan Steel Works, Tokai Carbon and Toyota Tsusho are declining almost 4 percent each, while Sumitomo Heavy Industries, Mitsubishi Motors, Furukawa Electric, Dowa Holdings, Mitsui & Co., Marubeni and Resonac Holdings are losing more than 3 percent each.

In economic news, the value of core machinery orders in Japan was down a seasonally adjusted 0.3 percent on month in September, the Cabinet Office said on Thursday - coming in at 1,066.2 billion yen. That was shy of expectations for an increase of 1.3 percent following the 5.2 percent gain in August. On a yearly basis, orders rose 13.4 percent - again missing expectations for 13/7 percent and down from 18.6 percent in the previous month.

For the third quarter of 2026, orders were up 1.2 percent on quarter and 14.1 percent on year at 3,152.8 billion yen. For the fourth quarter of 2026, orders are forecast to rise 4.3 percent on quarter and 13.9 percent on year to 3,287.0 billion yen.

In the currency market, the U.S. dollar is trading in the lower 159 yen-range on Thursday.

On Wall Street, stocks turned in a relatively lackluster performance during trading on Wednesday after trending lower over the past several sessions. The Nasdaq and S&P 500 spent much of the day lingering near the unchanged line, although the narrower Dow showed a notable move to the downside.

The major averages eventually ended the day mixed. While the Nasdaq climbed 101.50 points or 0.4 percent to 24,429.88, the S&P 500 dipped 16.90 points or 0.2 percent to 7,323.63 and the Dow slumped 561.25 points or 1.1 percent to 50,198.17.

Meanwhile, the major European markets all moved to the downside on the day. While the U.K.'s FTSE 100 Index tumbled by 1.3 percent, the German DAX Index slumped by 1.2 percent and the French CAC 40 Index declined by 0.9 percent.

Crude oil prices tumbled on Wednesday following a report that U.S. crude oil inventories increased much more than expected in the last week. West Texas Intermediate crude for December delivery was down $2.92 or 3.4 percent to $83.09 a barrel.

data.title: Ondas’ Aston Martin F1 Deal Draws Retail Backlash As Investors Question Spending, Margins
data.description:
Key points:
  • Ondas has signed a multi-year partnership with Aston Martin’s Formula One team through 2029.
  • Branding will debut at the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix, with race-suit placements starting in 2027. 
  • Ondas’ Aston Martin partnership could add to expenses as it works toward profitability.

Ondas’ (ONDS) Formula One partnership with Aston Martin is raising fresh questions about its spending priorities, while an SEC filing allowing shareholders to resell 6,292 shares adds to investor concerns. With cash burn under scrutiny, retail traders are questioning whether the autonomous tech provider’s growth ambitions come at a high cost.

Ondas stock ticked 0.9% higher overnight Wednesday. The stock is on track for a third weekly loss.

Ondas’ Formula One Partnership Targets Technology Exchange

On Wednesday, Ondas said it has entered a multi-year global partnership with the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team, bringing the autonomous tech company into the world of Formula One through 2029.

The agreement centers on a shared focus on "Speed to Decision," highlighting how engineering, data analysis and quick execution can improve performance in demanding operating conditions.

Las Vegas will provide the first major showcase for the partnership. Ondas branding will appear on the front section of Aston Martin's race car during the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix. The company will also feature on team racing suits beginning with the 2027 season.

"Aston Martin Aramco gives Ondas global reach to engage customers, partners and investors, while creating opportunities for our teams to collaborate and share how advanced technology can help organizations operate with greater speed, precision and confidence."

Ondas’ Formula One Deal Raises Fresh Spending Concerns

Ondas’ latest partnership could increase spending on marketing, travel, hospitality and branding while the company is still struggling to become consistently profitable. The deal’s financial terms remain undisclosed, and it does not include any confirmed new revenue contracts. Investors question whether the spending could delay Ondas’ goal of achieving adjusted EBITDA profitability by third-quarter 2027.

Ondas’ Q3 2026 revenue doubled from Q2 to $167.5 million, boosted by strong sales of anti-drone systems and recent acquisition deals. However, its gross margin dropped to 21.8% from 43.1% in Q2 as costs rose and production faced challenges.

Ondas Registers Existing Shares For Potential Resale 

Also, Ondas has filed paperwork allowing certain existing shareholders to resell up to 6,292 shares of the company's common stock. The filing covers securities previously issued to those investors as part of an earlier purchase agreement and does not represent a new share issuance by the company.

What ONDS Retail Traders Are Saying 

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the stock declined to ‘bearish’ from ‘bullish’.

A user said, “$ONDS is burning money every quarter and they decide to sponsor a race car; now they r just toying with retail to their face .”

Another user said, “Imagine blowing up shareholder money on race car stickers I would be pissed.”

A third user said, “Looks like all the buying just gets sold into. That’s what you call delusion thanks, Erik. The only way the stock is gonna go up is if they get a deal in the works and need the investment bankers to move it higher just like they did before. Pathetic.

ONDS stock has crashed 54% year-to-date.

data.title: Wall Street Pledged to Mobilize $500 Billion for Nvidia-But Hasn't Put Up a Dime — WSJ
data.description:
By Jack Pitcher, Peter Rudegeair and Anissa Gardizy

Jensen Huang sensed the winds shifting against Nvidia this spring.

In June, Wall Street giants Apollo Global Management and Blackstone announced a megadeal to help Broadcom, one of Nvidia's main rivals, secure $35 billion of chip financing for Anthropic.

Huang, then chief executive, was irate, people close to the situation said. He'd been talking about a similar program and felt the progress was too slow, so he summoned several titans of Wall Street to California, the people said. Huang wanted a bigger deal and fast.

In August, he got pledges from several firms — Apollo, Blackstone, BlackRock, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR — to mobilize an astounding sum: $500 billion.

The announcement created the splash Huang wanted as he sat around a table with Goldman's David Solomon, Blackstone's Jonathan Gray and other financial executives for a live CNBC appearance. Solomon dubbed it a "pivotal moment of a historic AI investment cycle."

The wave of money was supposed to help Nvidia's startup customers — from OpenAI and Anthropic to smaller, weaker ones — finance the chips they needed to buy, keeping Nvidia's sales humming well into the future. They were seeking to turn chip financing into a standardized asset class.

But the promise was short on substance. To date, no capital has actually been deployed, according to people familiar with the matter. And investors are increasingly skeptical that the program will reach its lofty ambitions now that Huang has been ousted over a sex and suspected spy scandal that has engulfed Nvidia.

Nvidia had already begun to rein in the backstops and guarantees it uses to grease lending, partly under the skepticism of finance chief Colette Kress, who has now become the interim CEO. Those guarantees are crucial to Wall Street's willingness to finance the chips, and Kress on Tuesday signaled to investors that the company will be disciplined in the deals it supports.

"We are proud of the role that we have played so far in supporting the ecosystem," Kress said on a conference call about earnings. "We are rigorously evaluating future investments, commitments and guarantees."

Wall Street and Nvidia both still have lucrative reasons to make some financing work, even if the full $500 billion doesn't materialize.

Nvidia's sales and forecasts remained strong in its most recent quarter, but the questions about how its customers get financing to keep buying chips are central to investor and analyst opinions on the stock and its valuation.

A $1 trillion plan

Frustrated that Nvidia's valuation multiple was dropping at the start of the year despite jaw-dropping profit, Huang began to focus on levers he could pull, people familiar with his thinking said.

He had one big idea: a $1 trillion partnership with Wall Street partners, according to some of the people.

Nvidia had been in talks for months with financiers at Goldman Sachs, Blackstone and Apollo about how it could help backstop secured loans for its less creditworthy customers. But such deals can be complex, and talks were moving slowly. Goldman bankers and others in the consortium labored for weeks over the best structure to get investors comfortable with lending to Nvidia customers on the scale Huang was hoping for.

After Broadcom announced a similar deal, Huang injected more urgency.

Then The Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia was considering providing a $250 billion backstop for an OpenAI data center in Ohio. The next day, Nvidia shares fell by 5%, wiping out $250 billion in market value.

The market's negative reaction prompted Nvidia to rework its deal and cut its initial financial commitment to OpenAI in half, the Journal reported. News Corp, owner of The Wall Street Journal, has a content-licensing partnership with OpenAI.

Nvidia was concerned the market would think it was taking on too much risk and it wanted to signal that other investors were ready to help finance chips.

By early August, Nvidia brought BlackRock, Brookfield, and KKR into the fold on the chip financing program, people familiar with the matter said.

The half-trillion-dollar memorandum of understanding the firms signed was just a few pages that specified a fundraising target, the profile of target customers and that Nvidia would consider providing credit backstops on a case-by-case basis, people familiar with the matter said. The investment firms involved aren't committed to actually raising any money, and the $500 billion figure isn't meaningful, the people said.

The idea behind the agreement was to signal that financing will be available, and get major Wall Street partners thinking about how to solve a complex issue, the people said.

Analysts applauded the company's ability to move itself out of the center of financing its customers. But they were quick to note the aspirational nature of the firms' agreement to work together on raising $500 billion "over time."

The feasibility of the plan has run into hurdles in the months since, especially as lenders have cracked down on fueling the AI boom.

A major contention between the Wall Street side and Nvidia has been how much Nvidia was willing to backstop the clients it wanted the lenders to support.

Huang said in August that the credit support Nvidia was willing to provide would top out at 25% of the cost of a project. That is a lower level of backing than rivals agreed to. Broadcom provided a residual-value guarantee for about 85% of Project Big Sky, the $35 billion financing for Anthropic announced in June. For Project North Star, a $63 billion follow-up financing, Broadcom's residual-value guarantee covered a little under three-quarters of the transaction.

Credit markets have grown more skeptical of AI-linked borrowers with low credit ratings since early August, and investors have been pushing for a larger than 25% residual value guarantee to get comfortable with lending, people familiar with the matter said, a potential roadblock if Nvidia is pulling back support.

Talks are ongoing for the partnership's first chip-backed finance deal for an Nvidia customer, but nothing is expected to be completed before next year, some of the people said.

"There was a strong incentive for Nvidia as a business matter to get these projects off the ground," Apollo CEO Marc Rowan said on CNBC on Tuesday. "If that banking function, that guarantor function, gets taken away, access to capital for a large number of neoclouds is going to disappear."

Write to Jack Pitcher at jack.pitcher@wsj.com, Peter Rudegeair at peter.rudegeair@wsj.com and Anissa Gardizy at anissa.gardizy@wsj.com

data.title: The Jensen Huang Saga Has Reinvigorated Washington's China Hawks — WSJ
data.description:
By Heather Somerville and Amrith Ramkumar

A year ago, Jensen Huang called the term China hawk "a badge of shame" and "unpatriotic." His ouster from Nvidia, where he was co-founder and chief executive, is giving new momentum to policymakers who want to regulate artificial intelligence and establish more guardrails around U.S. business activity with China.

Claims that Nvidia customers funneled billions of dollars of sophisticated chips to Chinese AI companies have collided in recent days with a string of technological breakdowns — from a nationwide ground stop for airlines to bank-account glitches and money-transfer delays.

In recent weeks the Trump administration:

Released a new rule aimed at preventing China's AI industry from accessing computing power running on U.S. chips.

Supported efforts to advance legislation to restrict sales of advanced chips and chipmaking equipment to countries that pose security risks.

Fined a U.S. investment firm for funding a Chinese AI company.

Has weighed whether U.S. companies should disclose use of Chinese open-weight models.

Has considered new rules around Chinese equipment in U.S. data centers.

Together, the measures signal that Washington is moving away from the administration's pro-industry approach to tech policy that mostly relied on companies to balance their business interests and national security while selling sensitive technology.

"The more that changes, the less there's going to be an appetite to sell it. The whole Nvidia incident was an accelerant of this," said Saif Khan, founding director of the Center for Technology & Statecraft, who worked on tech policy in the Biden administration.

On Monday, before President Trump boarded Air Force One to meet with China's Xi Jinping this week in Shenzhen for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation meetings, he defended Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who has resisted restrictions that might anger China — despite opposition from Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and other officials.

But as political winds shift, Bessent, Secretary of State Marco Rubio and other administration players have advanced proposed rules in recent weeks that had been languishing, including the chip-export restrictions announced Monday.

Many businesses that realize a relationship with China, or an intermediary, could hurt them politically are paying more attention to those new policies and the threats from the incoming Democratic-run Congress than Trump's words, business advisers said.

"Companies that assumed the light-touch approach would hold through 2028 are going to have to recalibrate," said Joseph Hoefer, chief AI officer at lobbying firm Monument Advocacy, which represents companies including Netflix and Waymo. "National security gives all sides cover to deal in a way that just wasn't there before."

Getting tougher on China

For much of the past year, the Trump administration had adopted trade practices and rhetoric toward China that were largely focused on maintaining a detente with Beijing. Activities seen as antagonistic to China were largely delayed, scrapped or toned down as Trump tried to strengthen relations following Beijing's crushing export controls on rare earths, The Wall Street Journal has reported.

The approach frustrated China hawks on both sides of the aisle who have been calling for investigations into alleged chip smuggling in Southeast Asia, only to watch Huang deny that Nvidia had a diversion problem and lobby Trump directly for fewer regulations and more access to China. Lawmakers and Commerce Department staffers, some who were forced out for advocating for greater restrictions, also wanted the department to close loopholes that allowed Chinese companies to access computing power in other countries and have blamed the agency for not doing more, faster.

The recently released rule on chip exports makes it more difficult for Chinese companies to access computing power in Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Singapore while tightening restrictions on Chinese chip designers. It took effect immediately but companies have about 60 days to offer comments.

"There are those of us who wanted to have this regulation and now it's becoming obvious why we need to have it,'" said Sen. Pete Ricketts (R., Neb.), one of the lawmakers pushing for more chip-export restrictions. "This gives us more momentum to go back and do more restrictions." The administration is also weighing a new rule that would require U.S. companies to disclose which Chinese AI models they deploy — an effort to discourage the tools without banning them outright, people familiar with the matter said. Many top companies, including Airbnb and crypto firm Coinbase, use Chinese AI tools because they are often cheaper and easier to customize than models from OpenAI and Anthropic.

Democratic control

The Nvidia scandal unfolded amid long simmering worries about AI dominance. In addition to re-energizing Democrats, the scandal has emboldened the camp inside the Trump administration and around Washington that favors AI regulation.

Democrats who have promised to regulate AI, including Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D., Mass) and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D., N.Y.), are expected to keep up a drumbeat of criticism and questions around the close relationship Huang and other tech executives have with Trump and his advisers. Democrats who might not have taken such hawkish stances will now adopt them on many issues, a senior Democratic staffer said.

The hardened posture in Washington could throw a lifeline to the House Select Committee on China, which was created by a Republican-controlled House in 2023 and called for restrictions on companies such as Megaspeed, the Singapore-based Nvidia business partner accused of smuggling Nvidia chips to China. Alice Huang, the former top Megaspeed executive suspected of being a Chinese intelligence asset, had an affair with Jensen Huang.

But for much of the last two years, the committee has been sidelined as Trump stressed friendly relations with China. It was at risk of being disbanded by the incoming Democratic Congress, but the committee's odds look better now. Rep. Hakeem Jeffries, (D., N.Y.), the presumptive House speaker, is expected to make a determination after Thanksgiving.

H.K. Park, who leads the national security practice at Washington advisory firm Crumpton Global, said that since the Nvidia scandal broke, he had received triple the number of requests from companies to vet their suppliers, business partners and customers in Southeast Asia for any threats to national security. Corporate boards, largely from the tech industry, have hired the firm to check whether they have any exposure to a China-linked security risk. In some cases, companies are concerned about becoming the next target of a U.S. government investigation. Huang and Nvidia have been called to testify in front of congressional committees in the coming weeks.

Cloud-computing company Oracle recently canceled a $7 billion, five-year agreement to lease AI computing capacity to Chinese technology giant Tencent in Southeast Asia, after administration officials raised concerns about the deal, people familiar with the matter said.

Oracle didn't respond to a request for comment.

Write to Heather Somerville at heather.somerville@wsj.com and Amrith Ramkumar at amrith.ramkumar@wsj.com

data.title: How a Battered Industrial Corridor Beat the Odds and Reimagined Its Economy — WSJ
data.description:
By Arian Campo-Flores | Photography by Jeremy Lange for WSJ

GREENSBORO, N.C. — Kevin Baker called it the "global domination plan." The executive director of Piedmont Triad International Airport in Greensboro wanted to turn the small facility into a grand aerospace hub with an array of manufacturers that would spur the region's economy.

So about 15 years ago, the airport took a flier on a risky $350 million strategy to gobble up neighboring land, invest in expensive bridges, roadways and utility connections — and hope tenants would follow. When the pieces were in place, Baker and others pitched PTI at trade events like the Paris Air Show.

"We set out to make ourselves as ready as possible for companies that showed up," he said.

The gamble is paying off. Boom Supersonic — a Centennial, Colo.-based company that aims to build a supersonic passenger jet — has now completed construction of an aircraft manufacturing facility at the airport. The $500 million project is expected to create more than 1,750 jobs.

This summer, Long Beach, Calif.-based JetZero broke ground on a $4.7 billion production facility at the airport to manufacture a manta-ray-like passenger aircraft. The facility is slated to generate about 14,500 jobs.

Those successes are part of a broader transformation of the Piedmont Triad, a region once known for its textile, tobacco and furniture-making industries — until they were battered by globalization and offshoring in the 1990s and 2000s. Anchored by Greensboro, Winston-Salem and High Point, the Triad lost tens of thousands of jobs as companies closed or moved away. Downtowns fell into disrepair.

Within North Carolina, the region fell behind as Charlotte's financial hub and the Raleigh area's technology cluster helped those cities boom.

More recently, the Triad pulled off an unusual feat that has eluded many areas hit by deindustrialization: It reinvented its economy. The region is now a center for aerospace, advanced manufacturing, life sciences and logistics.

In the decade ending 2024, the Triad's population grew 7%, employment increased 16% and median household income jumped 48%, according to Carolina Demography, a unit of the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill.

This renaissance has faced setbacks, as some plans have fallen through. But the projects keep coming.

In November 2025, Toyota opened a battery manufacturing plant in Liberty, a small town southeast of Greensboro, which is expected to generate more than 5,000 jobs. A year earlier, Ziehl-Abegg — a German maker of ventilation systems in high demand by data centers — expanded into a highly automated plant in Winston-Salem and is projected to increase its workforce to about 1,000 in the next two years.

Developers and academic institutions turned former R.J. Reynolds Tobacco manufacturing plants in downtown Winston-Salem into a mixed-use district they call the Innovation Quarter. It now includes a cutting-edge research institute housing regenerative-medicine startups. A former hosiery mill in High Point was turned into Congdon Yards, with co-working spaces, business offices and an industrial-grade workshop for makers and designers.

Political and business leaders in the Triad say a high tolerance for risk helped. Economic-development groups rolled the dice with big public and private investments in land and infrastructure to try to lure new industries. City chambers of commerce in the Triad banded together to pitch the region collectively to companies, rather than competing against one another.

North Carolina's swing-state status, with a Democratic governor and Republican-led state Senate, has pushed the parties to work together on economic development, some officials say. Roy Cooper, a former two-term Democratic governor who won his U.S. Senate race earlier this month, is a moderate who has pitched his state as business-friendly.

The Triad's resurgence is helping turn North Carolina into a major draw. The state in recent years has bypassed much bigger Texas and Florida as a destination for net domestic migration — people arriving from other states minus those leaving to other states — according to the Census Bureau.

"The leaders there have done a fabulous job of transforming that economy," said Michael Walden, a professor emeritus of economics at North Carolina State University.

Affordability has helped, too: In the second quarter this year, the Triad's median home price was $304,000, compared with $409,000 in the Raleigh-area Research Triangle and $413,000 in the Charlotte area, said Tony Jarrett, a regional vice president at Howard Hanna Allen Tate Real Estate. The median home price in the U.S. as a whole was $408,000 in June, according to Redfin.

'We've got a problem'

Decades ago, the Triad's economy was humming.

Greensboro's textile industry made it the Denim Capital of the World, and Winston-Salem's tobacco manufacturing earned it the moniker Camel City, after the cigarette brand. High Point is still known as the Home Furnishings Capital of the World, though its furniture business is now centered on design rather than manufacturing.

Overseas competition badly hurt the domestic textile and furniture industries, and health concerns pummeled tobacco companies. The Greensboro and High Point areas lost more than 34,000 manufacturing jobs between 1990 and 2010, a 40% decline, while the Winston-Salem area shed more than 31,000, a 52% drop, according to Bureau of Labor Statistics data. The poverty rate in Winston-Salem climbed.

Toward the tail end of that period, "we were like, well damn, we've got a problem," said Stan Kelly, who was on the board of the Piedmont Triad Partnership, a regional economic development group. "And no one is going to fix our problem but us."

Business leaders in the region joined forces to raise money for economic studies aimed at finding ways to counteract the damage, Kelly said.

They concentrated on several large sites, including closed cigarette factories in Winston-Salem, that could be either developed or revitalized to attract new industries. They implored state officials to advocate for the area on trade missions.

When Christopher Chung became chief executive of the Economic Development Partnership of North Carolina in 2015, that message dominated his early conversations with Triad representatives. "Raleigh and Charlotte are getting all the wins," he said they told him. "We need you to think about this part of the state."

By that time, Baker's global domination plan was under way at the airport, one of the sites regional leaders were boosting. The airport had some momentum to build on, Baker thought, including recently added tenants such as a FedEx sorting facility and a Honda Aircraft plant that manufactures business jets.

Yet as the airport bought up land, it ran into an obstacle: a planned interstate nearby that would divide a swath of newly acquired property from the runways. Baker proposed building a bridge over the interstate to allow planes to taxi across, but that carried a $20 million price tag. Baker pressed his case with transportation and elected officials that the connection would be indispensable.

The airport also prepared the purchased land by grading it, hooking up utilities and building access roads. It did all this on spec with public money.

At the June groundbreaking for the JetZero plant, which will occupy more than 600 acres, Chief Executive Tom O'Leary cited the airport's foresight in amassing land and building the connecting bridge. "This is a real growth-oriented mindset," he said. "It really set Greensboro apart when we were searching for a home."

Another of JetZero's considerations was securing a workforce. The economic development team that wooed the company included Guilford Technical Community College, whose aviation program is located next to the airport.

North Carolina's community college system was a pioneer in collaborating with companies to develop training tailor-made for their needs. At GTCC, programs include composite technology, which is crucial for JetZero's lightweight, blended-wing aircraft, designed to use up to 50% less fuel than traditional commercial jets.

The college is building a new training facility and securing funding for an additional one. Together, those are projected to increase capacity for aviation students to more than 1,000 a year from 500 a year currently, said Anthony Clarke, GTCC's president.

Graduates of the college make up a sizable part of the workforce at Honda Aircraft, which makes a six-passenger jet and is preparing to manufacture a new 10-passenger one. The company plans to add more than 175 workers to its existing staff of about 1,000, said senior vice president Rich Richardson.

One of the college's former students is Jose Carrion, who moved to Greensboro from Methuen, Mass., in 2011 after hearing about job opportunities at Honda Aircraft. He's worked his way up from technician to manufacturing supervisor, and has benefited from the area's lower cost of living.

"We don't see ourselves living anywhere else," said Carrion, who is 36 and has five children.

About 30 miles southeast, in Liberty, a group including local governments, a railroad company and the Joseph M. Bryan Foundation, which focuses in part on economic development, began buying parcels of land in the 2010s to assemble a megasite. With automakers adding manufacturing plants in the Southeast, they hoped to lure one.

When a joint venture between Toyota and Mazda started looking for a location for an auto manufacturing plant, the group seized the opportunity. Their 1,800-acre Liberty site was a finalist in the selection process. But the joint venture chose Huntsville, Ala., instead.

Triad officials requested a debriefing on why they came up short. Over a two-hour lunch, one of the project consultants detailed a list of issues they needed to address.
